class.name: PSXMaterial3D
class.brief_description: A [StandardMaterial3D] with options for the PS1 renderer.
class.description: Works like [StandardMaterial3D] and adds a PSX group: dithering on or off for this material whatever the settings say, and subdivision off. To turn an existing material into one, choose [b]Convert to PSXMaterial3D[/b] in its menu in the inspector; its other properties are kept. Godot's own renderers ignore these options. With the PS1 renderer off, the material draws as a [StandardMaterial3D].

members.member: Whether the GPU's 4×4 ordered dither is used on this material's polygons. [constant DITHER_PROJECT] follows the [code]dither[/code] setting (project setting, [PSXSettings] node or [method PSX.set_setting]). On the PS1, dither is drawing state rather than part of a polygon, so a material that differs from the setting adds a drawing-mode command before and after each of its triangles. That costs little, but it is not free on large meshes.

[constant SUBDIVIDE_OFF] draws this material's meshes with their own triangles, without the splitting set by [member ProjectSettings.rendering/psx/subdivide_size]. Use it for meshes modelled with small, even triangles, or to keep the stretched textures and lighting of big polygons as a look. Large polygons near the camera may then be culled whole, as on the hardware.
